name: Sacheerome Ltd
tagline: Rs ~780 Cr NSE-SME B2B fragrance & flavour house on a 'brief-to-formulation' model -- ROCE ~36-39%, debt-free, ~24% revenue CAGR (Rs 64 Cr FY22 -> ~Rs 152 Cr FY26), OPM 13% -> 24%, Mukul Agarwal AIF holder -- genuine quality, but a small F&F TAM, a 4x capacity build well ahead of conservative guidance, and a stock already up ~3x from IPO
business_overview: Sacheerome (NSE SME, listed Jun-2025) is a specialised B2B fragrance & flavour (F&F) formulator founded 1992 by Mr. Manoj Arora. It works on a 'brief-to-formulation' model -- corporate FMCG and D2C brands hand over a brief, Sacheerome's R&D (~2.3% of sales) develops the fragrance / flavour, and once approved the formulation is locked into the client's product line, creating annuity-like recurring revenue. It is expanding capacity ~4x (7.6 -> 27.6 lakh kg) with ~Rs 184 Cr capex.
fundamentals_table: CFO consistently positive, often above operating profit
FY27 ~Rs 200 Cr, FY29 ~Rs 300 Cr revenue; ~25% EBITDA margin
~Rs 184 Cr for 4x capacity; ~Rs 47 Cr from accruals, rest IPO proceeds + ~Rs 60 Cr debt
fundamentals_narrative: This is a real quality small-cap: sustained ~24% revenue CAGR, OPM near-doubling to 24%, ROCE in the mid-to-high 30s, debt-free, and cash conversion above operating profit. The 'brief-to-formulation' lock-in is a genuine switching-cost mechanic and explains the margin premium over the larger, distributor-led S.H. Kelkar. Open questions from the VP thread: (1) capacity is going up 4x but management guides only ~Rs 250-300 Cr revenue by FY28-29 -- either the capex is imprudent or guidance is very conservative; (2) part of the recent margin gain came from a ~4% drop in employee expense, whose durability is unclear; (3) FMCG end-demand grows only ~10-12%, so above-market growth needs continuous new-brief / new-client wins; (4) ~Rs 60 Cr of the capex will be debt-funded. The stock has already re-rated ~3x from its Rs 102 issue price.

verdict_headline: A genuinely high-quality B2B fragrance formulator with a sticky model, but small TAM, a 4x build ahead of conservative guidance and a stock already up 3x -- 'neither', conviction Medium
verdict_reasoning: Aligns with the priority-1 'CDMO / specialty & aroma chemicals' theme (keywords include fragrance, aroma chemical, specialty chemical) -- but it was processed as a tier-4.5 external lead, not a Step-1 discovery theme hit, so theme-ranking is informational here. A value_chain block is included because the deep read made the position clear.

four_box score 2.5 -> 'neither'. tailwind yes (F&F premiumisation, D2C brand proliferation, import substitution from global majors -- a real multi-year pull), tam weak (Indian F&F market is a few thousand crore; a 10x-in-2-3-yr from ~Rs 152 Cr revenue would need ~Rs 500 Cr+ revenue by FY28, far above management's own ~Rs 250-300 Cr guide), moat weak (formulation lock-in and sustained high ROCE are convincing, but it is a small player with modest R&D intensity and unproven durability at scale), valuation weak (~26x FY26 earnings after a ~3x re-rating -- priced as a quality compounder). No written exception taken: valuation box is not 'yes' and guided growth is good but not 'un-ignorable'.

Conviction Medium (not lower): the business quality -- ROCE mid-30s, debt-free, sticky annuity model, cash conversion, a marquee AIF holder and an active thoughtful thread -- clearly stands above the rest of this batch. It is a quality small-cap worth tracking, not a screen buy and not a 10x case at this size and price. Re-check after two-plus post-expansion quarters show utilisation of the new capacity and whether guidance proves conservative.

value_chain.position: B2B fragrance & flavour formulator sitting between aroma-chemical / essential-oil suppliers (inputs) and FMCG / D2C brand owners (customers); 'brief-to-formulation' R&D partner rather than a commodity compound seller
value_chain.bottleneck_node: formulation IP + client-approved spec lock-in (the formulation, once designed into a brand's SKU, is costly for the brand to re-qualify away from)
value_chain.note: Sacheerome is adding ~4x capacity; larger domestic peer S.H. Kelkar is distributor-led and margin-pressured on raw-material volatility. Sacheerome's edge is the direct-to-brand formulation model, not scale -- durability of that edge as it scales is the key question.

four_box.note: tailwind=yes (F&F premiumisation + D2C brand proliferation + import substitution, priority-1 aroma-chemicals theme). tam=weak (Indian F&F market a few thousand crore; 10x-in-2-3-yr needs ~Rs 500 Cr+ revenue by FY28 vs management's ~Rs 250-300 Cr guide). moat=weak (formulation lock-in + sustained ~36% ROCE are real, but small player, modest R&D intensity, durability at scale unproven). valuation=weak (~26x FY26 earnings after a ~3x re-rating). Score 2.5 -> neither (no written exception).
